scope: The spec provenance matrix and the issue-link provenance model, with issue_id held as an opaque external payload. Belongs here: the provenance matrix rows and their sort/render; the **Issues:** role:ID parse into (req_id, issue_id, role); the doctrine that issue_id is opaque — projected only, never a PK/FK/UNIQUE/index/JOIN key. Does not belong here: the tracker fetch/cache that resolves an issue id to a title (→ TRK); requirement identity/routing (issue ids are provenance, never identity). Boundary case: a KEY-NNN-shaped issue id stays an opaque string in PROV and is never resolved against the requirements table.

requirements.statement: spec provenance treats every issue_id as an opaque payload — never a PK, FK, UNIQUE, index, or JOIN key — so an issue link can never silently become an identity or routing construct.
requirements.why: If an issue id became a join or routing key, an issue-link collision would silently reroute a requirement's provenance to the wrong requirement — corrupting the audit trail the provenance matrix exists to preserve.

requirements.statement: When resolved issue data is served from an expired cache after a failed refresh, spec provenance shall label it stale in both text and JSON output.
requirements.why: An old tracker title rendered as current is a quiet lie — degraded data must say it is degraded.

requirements.statement: When an authoring command is run with an issue flag, the spec CLI shall record the ticket id as provenance on the entry — created on a new requirement, supersedes-via on a superseded predecessor, amends-via on an amendment — never as identity or routing.
requirements.why: The engine warned about missing supersedes-via provenance while offering no way to write it — provenance the tool demands but cannot record is provenance that never exists.
